verdict.rationale: Cal.com documents a self-hostable, 100% MIT-licensed edition (Cal.diy) that runs without a license key, so self-hosting from source under an open-source license is supported. However, Cal.diy is a fork with enterprise code removed: community reports say Teams, Organizations, Workflows and SSO are gone, public Docker images are being discontinued, and the edition is recommended only for personal, non-production use. That means it is not the full scheduling engine. Missing for 10: the full engine (team/org/workflow features) under the open-source license, an official prebuilt container image, and production-grade self-host support.

support.subject: As a developer, I can self-host the full scheduling engine from source or a container image under an open-source license

citations.quote: Cal.diy is 100% MIT-licensed with no proprietary "Enterprise Edition" features. It's designed for individuals and self-hosters who want full control over their scheduling infrastructure
a fork of Cal.com with all enterprise/commercial code removed.
No license key required — Everything works out of the box, no Cal.com account or license needed
Cal.com's differentiators are the self-hostable MIT edition (Cal.diy)
